To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. the judgements of patients and therapists for change are not correlated; 2. the judgements are correlated to different information; 3. the judgements can be influenced by different variables; 4. patients tend to rate their own change more positive than their therapists.
the judgements of psychotherapist and patients about change are only weakly correlated and that there are several predictive variables for discrepancies of judgements for change.
the psychotherapist tends to make a more negative judgement than the patient, that the correlation between both judgements is low and that predictive variables are age and sex of the patient.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of different judgements for therapeutic change.
the problem of how to measure therapeutic change.
the question, which variables influence the discrepancy of the judgements of the patient and psychotherapist for change.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the judgements of psychotherapists are influenced by different factors than the judgement of their patients.
psychotherapists should be cautious to judge the therapeutic success by their own subjective rating.
there is no common ground of information between subjective ratings of patients and therapists, although the categories are identical.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the psychotherapist and the patient focus on different information when they evaluate the therapeutic progress.
the psychotherapie has to be adapted to the individual patient, because different patients have different needs.
the psychotherapist should consider the patient's judgement for change as well as the judgement of the patient.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no single, simple measure of therapeutic change.
the patient is the expert for his own change.
we have to be aware that the patient and the therapist focus on different information when they judge the change.
